title: Residual U(1) exactly explains candidate 48's duplicated 2+2 vector-seed Hessian split

claim.statement: The v646 anisotropy in both seeded SO(4) vectors is precisely the decomposition into the fixed and rotating planes of the unique compact U(1) generator that stabilizes the canonical candidate-48 vacuum and preserves the 102-coordinate scalar ansatz.
claim.implication: Candidate 48 is quadratically covariant under the residual U(1), but not under the compact Lorentz SO(4) required for direct Spin(2,3) completion.

interpretation: The twofold degeneracies are representation-theoretic U(1) multiplets rather than numerical accidents.
The charged rotating plane is much lighter than the neutral fixed plane by a factor of about 44.34 in the Hessian coefficient.
The identical pattern in the inequivalent SO(5) irreps 10 and 14 suggests a shared carrier-level origin, while their zero cross-Hessian respects the irrep separation.
A symmetry-restoring deformation must close a gap of 0.562390314491462 per vector sector without inducing forbidden 10-to-14 mixing.
falsifiers: Failure of scalar-span closure under the stabilizer would invalidate the charge assignment; the measured residual is 8.52e-16.
A nonzero U(1)-invariance residual would invalidate the plane interpretation; both are below 3e-16.
The result concerns the canonical vacuum and the established residual generator; other vacua can rotate the charge planes.
nextBranches: Construct the minimal positive semidefinite projector counterterm that raises only the charged plane to the neutral coefficient.
Test whether that counterterm can arise from the omitted nine SO(5) response generators or necessarily requires completed scalar descendants.
Classify the five accidental moduli under the same U(1).
